data.title: SpaceX Logs 56 Canadian Lobbying Reports in 2026 Despite Ottawa’s Starlink Concerns
data.description:
SpaceX has continued to engage extensively with Canadian government officials in 2026, even as Prime Minister Mark Carney has outlined plans to reduce Canada’s dependence on Starlink.

Federal lobbying records show SpaceX representatives have engaged with Canadian officials on 37 separate occasions this year, with the company and its consultants submitting a combined 56 reports to Canada’s Registry of Lobbyists.

The House of Commons and Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) were the most frequently contacted institutions. SpaceX also engaged with the Prime Minister’s Office and several other federal departments.

Among those communications was an August 28 technical briefing with ISED officials, during which SpaceX submitted a 10-page assessment of how its frequency use at Janet, Alberta, and Saint-Laurent, Quebec, could affect other services.

Canada Seeks to Reduce Its Reliance on Starlink

The lobbying activity has continued since Carney’s September 23 interview with The New York Times, in which he said, “Starlink, we will diversify away from, no question.” The most recent communication recorded in the registry took place on November 13 with MP Lori Idlout and two House of Commons staff members.

data.title: Tesla Surpasses 1,000 Cybercab Registrations in Texas After Record Jump
data.description:
Tesla has surpassed 1,000 Cybercab registrations in Texas, adding another 285 Cybercabs on Thursday and breaking its previous single-day record set just over a week ago.

According to the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV), Tesla now has 1,841 vehicles registered for automated operation in the state. Based on vehicle identification numbers (VINs), that includes 1,107 Cybercabs and 734 Model Ys. The number of registered Model Ys remained unchanged.

All 285 newly added Cybercabs are designated as 2027 model year vehicles. Tesla’s registered Cybercab fleet now consists of 573 model year 2026 vehicles and 534 model year 2027 vehicles.

The latest additions also extend Tesla’s lead over Waymo in Texas. The tracker currently lists Waymo with 1,409 registered vehicles, putting Tesla ahead by 432 vehicles.

Earlier this month, Tesla was just three vehicles shy of matching Waymo’s registered fleet, with 1,282 vehicles compared to Waymo’s 1,285. Tesla now accounts for 44.9% of all vehicles on the state’s automated motor vehicle register.

Tesla’s Cybercab fleet is also expanding beyond Austin, with Tesla launching Cybercab rides in Dallas on November 19, making it the second city after Austin where customers can request rides in the two-seater. The vehicles deployed in Dallas are also a newer iteration, known as Cybercab V1.5, featuring factory-integrated Starlink hardware for satellite connectivity.

The statewide registration figures do not reveal how many of the latest additions are destined for either city.

data.title: Elon Musk Pledges to Give U.S. Children SpaceX Shares Every Year
data.description:
Elon Musk has expanded his pledge to donate SpaceX shares to American children, saying he will personally give them SpaceX shares not once, but every year.

In a post on X on Thursday, Musk said he would add another share every year, on top of the share donation he previously announced.

“I will be donating another share of SpaceX to all kids in America every year,” Musk wrote.

The announcement comes just one day after SpaceX announced it would issue one new Class A share to every Trump Account that is currently active, with Musk personally matching the company’s contribution.

Trump Accounts are tax-advantaged savings accounts for American children under 18 who have a Social Security number.

According to figures released by the White House in October, almost 70 million accounts had been opened, with more than 60 million set up through automatic enrolment. The company said the planned gifts depend on third-party and government approvals.

Musk first announced his plans to donate SpaceX shares in October, describing the initial gift as the “first of many.” Thursday’s announcement marks the first time Musk has specified that the donations will be made annually.

Meanwhile, Musk has also provided a timeline for the distribution of the initial two shares, with the company’s contribution expected to arrive before the end of 2026.

“The share from SpaceX will be transferred next month. The share directly from me will be transferred when my lockup expires in June next year,” Musk said on Wednesday evening.

data.title: Ontario Premier urges B.C. to immediately scrap EV sales mandate
data.description:
Ontario Premier Doug Ford said on X on Thursday that he has written to British Columbia Premier Lorne Doerkson, urging him to immediately follow through on his promise to scrap the province’s electric vehicle (EV) sales mandate, citing concerns over Canadian auto industry jobs.

In the letter attached to that post, Ford argued that the mandate places additional financial pressure on Canadian automakers already dealing with U.S. tariffs.

Ford’s letter comes after Doerkson has already taken the first step towards ending the mandate, directing Environment Minister Áʼa:líya Warbus in her mandate letter on Tuesday to introduce legislation ending the zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) sales quota.

However, Ford is pushing for the new B.C. government to move quickly, arguing that domestic policies are making it more expensive for Canadian automakers to compete with their international rivals.

“As we work together to protect Canadian workers in the face of tariffs, I urge you to follow through on your commitment to scrap this harmful policy at the earliest opportunity,” Ford wrote.

Ford also wrote that a swift repeal of B.C.’s mandate would help support efforts to save 2,000 jobs at the Stellantis assembly plant in Brampton, which he said are hanging in the balance.

In a separate Ontario statement issued Thursday, Ford joined Unifor National President Lana Payne in calling on Ottawa to exempt Canadian automakers from greenhouse gas emissions non-compliance penalties.

British Columbia’s previous government had already scaled back its ZEV sales mandate in April 2026, lowering the 2035 target to 75% and dropping the earlier plan to prohibit new gasoline and diesel vehicle sales.

That 75% target remains in effect under the province’s Zero-Emission Vehicles Act. No legislation to end the mandate has been introduced, with a bill expected during the spring legislative sitting.

data.title: Starlink offers 50% off Residential service in Canada and U.S. for Black Friday
data.description:
Starlink is offering 50% off Residential service in Canada and the United States as part of their Black Friday deal, after an earlier 30% offer on Residential and Roam plans that was also set to end November 30.

How the deal works

According to an email Starlink sent to customers, new subscribers who order by Monday, November 30, will pay half price for their first six months, with plans starting at C$37.50 in Canada or US$50 per month in the U.S.

There’s a catch worth knowing about. The offer is only available in some areas, so the price you see depends on where you’re signing up for the service. You’ll have to enter your address on Starlink’s site to find out what you qualify for.

Who it makes sense for

Residential is Starlink’s home internet plan, and it’s built for places where cable or fibre hasn’t arrived yet. Starlink says speeds can top 400 Mbps, but that’s a best-case number, and things can slow down when a lot of people in your area are online at once.

If you mostly want internet on the road or at a campsite, Roam plans are priced separately and start at C$75 a month in Canada.

You can check what’s available at your address on starlink.com. Starlink still offers a 30-day trial, so if it doesn’t work out, you can send it back for a full refund.

data.title: Tesla Rolls Out Manual Battery Preconditioning With Software Update 2026.44.3.1
data.description:
Tesla has begun rolling out software update 2026.44.3.1, giving owners the ability to manually precondition their vehicle’s battery ahead of a fast charging session, potentially reducing the amount of time spent charging.

Until now, Tesla owners have largely relied on the vehicle’s navigation system to automatically precondition the battery when routing to a Supercharger or compatible third-party fast charging station.

The new feature gives owners more control over when battery preconditioning begins, including the ability to start the process remotely before even getting into their vehicle.

How Manual Battery Preconditioning Works

Battery temperature plays an important role in determining how quickly an electric vehicle (EV) can charge. A cold battery cannot accept power at the same rate as one that has reached its optimal charging temperature, something particularly noticeable during the winter months.

According to the 2026.44.3.1 release notes, Tesla recommends starting battery preconditioning about one hour before a planned fast charging session. Once the battery reaches its optimal temperature, the vehicle will maintain it for 30 minutes.

Owners can also activate the feature remotely by opening the Tesla mobile app, navigating to the Charging section and selecting “Precondition for Fast Charging.” The feature requires mobile app version 4.63.0 or later.

This will be particularly useful for owners making short trips to nearby fast chargers, where the vehicle would otherwise have limited time to bring the battery up to its optimal temperature before arriving.

Benefits Beyond Fast Charging

Manual battery preconditioning could also be useful during the winter months, even when owners aren’t planning to fast charge. Warming the battery before leaving, particularly while the vehicle is plugged in at home, could help improve regenerative braking and reduce the amount of battery energy needed for heating while driving.

However, heating the battery to its optimal fast charging temperature may consume more energy than necessary for everyday driving.

The update began rolling out on Thursday, with data from TeslaFi showing one completed installation and five pending installations. The first recorded installation was on a Model Y Performance in Austria.

data.title: Vegas Loop Set to Double Network With 14 New Stations [Video]
data.description:
The Boring Company has shared a first look at its latest Vegas Loop expansion, with 14 new stations set to open alongside a new pair of tunnels from the Westgate Resort to a station opposite the Thomas & Mack Center at UNLV.

According to Vegas Loop on Thursday, the new twin tunnels span 2.3 miles (3.7 km), connecting the Westgate Resort to a station by the Thomas & Mack Center at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas.

The accompanying video shows a drive through the colourfully lit underground tunnels, passing through the Hughes Center station before emerging at 4744 Paradise Road.

The Boring Company’s website currently lists seven of the upcoming stations by name, including Virgin, Hughes Center, 4744 Paradise, Renaissance Hotel, Hyatt Place, Stirling Club, and The Collective.

Officials had hoped to open the expansion before the Las Vegas Grand Prix. However, as of November 19, Clark County had yet to issue the required temporary certificate of occupancy (via Las Vegas Review-Journal).

The new tunnels also bring the underground network closer to Harry Reid International Airport. The Vegas Loop already offers rides to and from the airport, although those trips currently include a combination of underground tunnels and surface streets.

The Boring Company has now transported more than four million passengers through its 14 operational stations, which include a North Strip stop at Sahara, with trip times ranging between two and eight minutes. The company is targeting 28 operational stations by the end of 2026.

Las Vegas and Clark County have already approved a much larger network, consisting of 68 miles (109 km) of underground tunnels connecting 123 stations.

data.title: Starlink could come to BC Ferries under new government mandate
data.description:
British Columbia’s new Conservative government has instructed its transportation minister to bring high-speed Wi-Fi to BC Ferries passengers, following the ferry operator’s earlier testing of SpaceX’s Starlink satellite internet service for crew members.

In a mandate letter issued on Tuesday, Premier Lorne Doerkson outlined several priorities for Minister of Transportation and Infrastructure Trevor Halford, including improving internet connectivity for ferry passengers.

Specifically, the letter directs Halford to “deliver reliable high-speed Wi-Fi on major routes and terminals through competitive private-sector procurement.”

While the letter does not name a preferred provider or set a timeline for introducing the service, BC Ferries already has experience with Starlink.

Starlink already being tested on BC Ferries

Since December 2024, BC Ferries has been testing Starlink on a limited number of vessels to address connectivity gaps for its crews.

That program is still ongoing. As recently as September 2026 a passenger shared a photo on Reddit showing Starlink’s Flat High Performance maritime terminals installed on a BC Ferries vessel.

Starlink is not the only option BC Ferries has been considering. In March 2025, the company said it was exploring Canadian satellite internet alternatives amid the Canada-U.S. tariff dispute at the time.

However, that procurement process was intended to address operational communications and safety needs, rather than provide internet access to passengers.

Bringing Wi-Fi back for passengers

BC Ferries previously offered Wi-Fi on several of its busiest routes, but discontinued the service in July 2021 after passengers found it slow and unreliable.

According to BC Ferries’ website, Wi-Fi remains unavailable onboard its vessels, although the company is currently expanding free wireless access at some terminals on the Central and North Coast.

Meanwhile, other ferry operators have already adopted Starlink for passenger use, including the Alaska Marine Highway System, which installed the satellite internet service on its MV Columbia in December 2024.

data.title: Tesla HW3 FSD Claim Surpasses 9,500 Participants Across 41 Countries
data.description:
A Dutch initiative that began earlier this year to organize Tesla Hardware 3 (HW3) owners for potential legal action has grown to more than 9,500 participants, including dozens of Canadians.

According to the HW3 Claim website, as of Thursday morning there were 9,558 verified participants across 41 countries, representing 15.9 million euros (C$24.8 million) in reported Full Self-Driving (FSD) purchases.

Among those are 50 Canadian participants who collectively report spending more than $280,000 on FSD.

The initiative has grown steadily since the summer, with a June 18, 2026 update reporting nearly 7,000 sign-ups, increasing to 8,668 verified participants by November 6, 2026.

Launched by Dutch Tesla owner and entrepreneur Mischa Sigtermans, HW3 Claim is preparing a collective legal action against Tesla’s Dutch entities under the country’s Mass Damage Settlement Act, after Tesla rejected two formal notices.

The initiative is seeking refunds for owners who paid for FSD, as well as compensation for the loss in value of their vehicles, including those whose cars are equipped with HW3 but who did not buy FSD.

While the Netherlands became the first European Union (EU) country to approve FSD on April 10, 2026, that approval only covers vehicles equipped with Hardware 4 (HW4).

Tesla has released a separate FSD V14 Lite software version for HW3 vehicles, although that software is not part of the Dutch approval.

For Canadian owners, however, the initiative currently serves primarily as a worldwide registry, with the proposed Dutch legal action unlikely to cover vehicles bought from a non-Dutch Tesla entity.

In its November 6, 2026 update, HW3 Claim said preparations were nearly complete and external funding was in its final stages. A lawsuit has not yet been filed.

data.title: Ontario opens HOV lanes to drivers without green plates during off-peak hours
data.description:
Ontario is opening high-occupancy vehicle (HOV) lanes to drivers travelling alone during off-peak hours, giving more motorists access to lanes now reserved for carpools and eligible green-plated vehicles.

According to the Ontario government, the changes will take effect on January 1, 2027, allowing drivers travelling alone to use HOV lanes without a special permit during designated hours.

Under the new rules, solo drivers may use the lanes on weekdays between 10 a.m. and 2 p.m., and overnight from 8 p.m. until 6 a.m.

Weekend access will also be expanded, with solo drivers allowed on the lanes between 9 p.m. and 9 a.m. on Saturdays and Sundays.

Outside those hours, existing HOV lane restrictions will continue to apply, requiring at least two occupants in most passenger vehicles. Eligible green-plated vehicles, along with buses, licensed taxis, motorcycles and emergency vehicles, remain among the current exemptions.

Solo passenger vehicles will not need a special permit in those off-peak windows. However, high-occupancy toll (HOT) permit holders will still be able to use the eligible lanes when solo access is otherwise limited.

The HOT permit program currently applies to eligible sections of the Queen Elizabeth Way (QEW), Highway 403 and Highway 410, allowing approved solo drivers to use those lanes during peak periods.

Ontario’s current HOV lane regulation already allows eligible green-plated vehicles to use the lanes with a single occupant at any time. Wednesday’s announcement does not specify whether that exemption will change.

Trucks and other commercial vehicles longer than 6.5 metres will still not be allowed to use HOV lanes, including in the new off-peak windows.

The government says its traffic modelling shows that letting more drivers into the lanes during quieter periods would ease congestion in the HOV lanes and in the general traffic lanes.
